messages:
alex: Heads up — quick proposal for splitting the global KV cache into segmented namespaces (per-tenant + hot-prefix lanes). Want a sanity check before I write the full RFC. TL;DR: lightweight segment descriptors in meta-store, two-phase ownership handoff, soft quotas + hot-lane promotion.

maya: can you drop a tiny diagram or pseudocode? not fully following what a 'segment descriptor' carries.

alex: pseudocode sketch:
```
struct Segment { prefix_hash, owner_node, gen }
// migrate flow
write Segment(new_owner, gen+1) -> CAS against expected gen
wait for ack from old_owner to drain inflight
mark old_owner drained -> complete
```
The CAS + gen gives us single-writer guarantees for ownership changes.

jin: main worry is concurrent migrates where two nodes think they won. CAS helps but what about network partitions? could see split-brain briefly.

alex: agreed. plan is CAS in etcd (meta-store) + short takeover timeout if owner unresponsive. takeover requires proof of unreachable + higher gen write. losers detect gen mismatch and back off.

laura: timeout-based takeovers make me nervous for R-A-W correctness. how do we avoid stale reads being served during a transfer?

alex: we pin writes to the primary owner until the change commits. reads consult local ownership-view (updated via watch). on gen mismatch readers invalidate local cache and fetch authoritative KV. practically: only transient extra miss on first post-transfer read.

sam: does that add a metastore RTT on first access to every prefix? adds latency risk.

alex: only on transfers. steady-state reads hit local map updated via watch stream -> no RTT in the hot path.

rik: eviction interaction question: if hot-lane prefixes fill their quota, how do we pick evict candidates? we need to consider request criticality (latency-sensitive vs batch) + size.

maya: suggestion: per-seg weighted score = access_rate * hotness_weight / size, combined with a short LRU window for new keys. avoids evicting tiny but hot entries.

jin: also need an explicit pin API for long-lived pinned entries (streaming + checkpoints). pinned items should be exempt from normal eviction but have TTL and admin revoke.

anna: ops checklist/metrics we should add: seg_owner_changes, seg_conflicts, eviction_reclaims, pin_count, wrong_owner_serves, migrate_latency. alerts on seg_conflicts > X/hour.

deploy-bot: seg-refactor branch deployed to staging at 2025-11-14T16:02Z :rocket:

alex: migration rollout plan (phased):
  1) enable seg-metadata watch-only (no transfers) -> gather owner-change metrics
  2) allow segment creation but no transfers (exercise creation path)
  3) migrate low-traffic prefixes in batches -> validate invariants
  4) enable transfers with low concurrency, monitor seg_conflicts/eviction_reclaims
  5) ramp and enable hot-lane promotion heuristics
If conflicts > threshold during step 4, rollback to step 1.

laura: rollback strategy question: if we abort mid-transfer, how do nodes reconcile partially moved segments?

alex: rollback flips system to "watch-only" mode. nodes detect gen mismatch and will invalidate affected keys; old and new owners coordinate a full invalidation pass. we also have a graceful-freeze API to reject new transfers during reconciliation.

sam: client-facing API changes? prefer none. we should keep protocol server-only and expose a compatibility flag so older workers still work during rollout.

maya: add to CI: chaos test that kills owner mid-transfer + concurrent writes/reads to ensure no duplication and read-after-write preserved. also a perf test to measure extra invalidation cost.

alex: will add chaos + perf tests to the RFC and include dashboard widgets for the metrics anna listed. thanks — I'll draft the RFC with the pseudocode, migration steps, and required metrics/alerts.

jin: one last nit: we should quantify expected window of double-serving (if any) in the document — ops will want an SLO delta estimate.

alex: good call, will add numbers and rollback thresholds.

maya: :thumbsup: good iteration.

alex: thanks everyone, PR incoming.
